problem: The rate of increase ${E}^{′}(t)$ of the average monthly cost of electricity in a particular region varies according to the differential equation ${E}^{′}(t)=0.02E(t),$ where $t$ is the time, in years, since the year $2017.$ In $2021,$ the average monthly cost was $$124.50.$ What was the average monthly cost of electricity in $2017?$
worked_solution:
The general solution to the given differential equation is

$$
E(t)={E}_{0}\,{e}^{0.02t},
$$

where ${E}_{0}$ is the average monthly cost of electricity in $2017.$

We are given that the monthly residential electricity cost was $$124.50$ in $2021,$ so after $t=4$ years. Hence, substituting $t=4$ and $E(4)=124.50$ into our general solution and solving for ${E}_{0},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}E(4) & ={E}_{0}\,{e}^{0.02\cdot 4} \\ 124.50 & ={E}_{0}\,{e}^{0.08} \\ {E}_{0} & =\frac{124.50}{{e}^{0.08}} \\  & ≈114.93\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest cent.

Therefore, the average monthly cost in $2017$ was $$114.93.$
